Users in Campus 2 VLAN 5 (PC1 at 10.5.0.1, PC2 at 10.5.0.2,
PC5 at 10.5.0.5) say they cannot reach anything outside their
own subnet. They can still ping each other. Campus 2 VLAN 6
users (PC3, PC4) are unaffected and have full connectivity.
Identify the fault.

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: sshswitch br_v5 SVI (10.5.0.254/24)
Mechanism: sshswitch is the multilayer switch that provides
  L3 gateways for Campus 2 VLANs 5, 6, 100, 200. PCs in
  VLAN 5 (PC1, PC2, dc_pc5) use 10.5.0.254 as their default
  gateway. When the br_v5 bridge interface goes down, the
  SVI IP becomes unreachable; packets from PCs to off-subnet
  destinations have no working next hop. VLAN 6 PCs are
  unaffected because their gateway lives on br_v6.
Localization: sshswitch
Root cause: br_v5 bridge interface is administratively down
  on sshswitch
Fix: `ip link set br_v5 up` on sshswitch
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set br_v5 up` on sshswitch
scoring_axes: must-identify-device: sshswitch (not the access switch switch4)

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The Layer 3 VLAN 5 bridge interface `br_v5` on `sshswitch`, which holds the inter-VLAN gateway address `10.5.0.254/24` for Campus 2 VLAN 5.

**Mechanism:** `sshswitch` is a combined L2/L3 device that terminates multiple campus VLANs. It presents a bridge interface per VLAN (`br_v5` for VLAN 5, `br_v6` for VLAN 6, etc.) and routes between them toward `router17` via a bonded uplink. The `br_v5` bridge is in state `DOWN` (`<BROADCAST,MULTICAST>` — no `UP` or `LOWER_UP` flags, carrier collisions = 0). Because the bridge is down, it cannot respond to ARP requests for `10.5.0.254`. VLAN 5 hosts (pc1, pc2, dc_pc5) send ARP for their default gateway and receive no reply; the Linux kernel on each host self-generates an ICMP "Destination Host Unreachable," which is exactly what was observed in the direct-IP probe from pc1. Simultaneously, the upstream routers have no reachable route to `10.5.0.0/24` (the interface is down), so they return "Destination Net Unreachable" when reverse-probed from pc10.

**Localization:** `sshswitch`, bridge interface `br_v5` (IP `10.5.0.254/24`). The peer VLAN 6 bridge `br_v6` (`10.6.0.254/24`) is fully `UP,LOWER_UP`, explaining why VLAN 6 users (pc3, pc4) are completely unaffected.

**Root cause:** The `br_v5` bridge interface on `sshswitch` has been administratively brought down, eliminating the VLAN 5 gateway and isolating all VLAN 5 hosts from inter-subnet traffic.

**Fix:** Run `ip link set br_v5 up` on `sshswitch` to restore the VLAN 5 gateway interface.

Directly recommends bringing the br_v5 interface up on sshswitch (ip link set br_v5 up), which matches the expected remediation.
